item.title: An axiom of unique reflection
item.description: arXiv:2611.07099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize neutral planes by three metric conditions: existence of geodesics, side-side-side congruence, and uniqueness of reflection.
item.dc:creator: Nina Lebedeva, Anton Petrunin

item.title: The dimension-free threshold for maximal sections of $\ell_p$
item.description: arXiv:2611.07619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of a sharp threshold $p_0 \approx 26.265\ldots$, such that for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p\geq p_0$, the volume maximizing section of the unit ball of $\ell_p^n$ is the section with Ball's hyperplane $(\frac{e_1+e_2}{\sqrt{2}})^\perp$, whereas for $p\in(2,p_0)$ the asymptotic maximizer as the ambient dimension $n\to\infty$ is the hyperplane orthogonal to the diagonal vector $\frac{e_1+\cdots+e_n}{\sqrt{n}}$.
item.dc:creator: Silouanos Brazitikos, Alexandros Eskenazis

item.title: A diameter-one set in $\mathbb{R}^5$ that cannot be covered by six diameter-one balls
item.description: arXiv:2611.08198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a compact set of diameter $1$ in $\mathbb{R}^5$ which cannot be covered by six Euclidean balls of diameter $1$. Its convex hull is a full-dimensional convex body satisfying the same property. Moreover, a finite subset of diameter $1$ cannot be covered by six closed balls even when their radius is increased to $0.50001$. The compact set is the quadratic image of the unit sphere in the space of symmetric $3\times3$ matrices of trace zero. A hypothetical cover leads to twelve spherical ellipses covering ${\mathbb S}^2$ and arranged in six antipodal pairs. Using Euler's formula, we replace them by twelve pentagonal regions contained in the ellipses. An area estimate then gives a contradiction.
item.dc:creator: A. Arman, A. Bondarenko, A. Prymak, D. Radchenko

item.title: Pappus's hexagon theorem for geodesic curves in $\SLR$ geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.08234v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we continue our investigation of the structure of Thurston geometries with non-constant curvature. We generalize the notion of cylinders, prove that they contain the types of geodesic curves. Moreover, we formulate and prove a statement analogous to Pappus's hexagon theorem for $\SLR$ geometry.
item.dc:creator: Jen\H{o} Szirmai

item.title: On Grassmann $4$-designs
item.description: arXiv:2611.08047v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that there is a unique tight $4$-design in the real Grassmannian $G_{2,4}$, up to the action of $O(4)$. Using symmetric association schemes, we also construct an $N$-point $4$-design in $G_{2,4}$ for every even integer $N\geq10$. For symmetric association schemes of order less than $21$, we classify the pairs of rank-three primitive idempotents defining injective maps into $G_{2,4}$; their images are Grassmannian $4$-designs precisely for four schemes of order $16$.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Samy Baladram, Ryutaro Misawa, Akihiro Munemasa

item.title: Closed-form solution for semi-symmetric folding of waterbomb tessellations
item.description: arXiv:2611.08050v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rigid-origami folding has versatile applications in the fields of architecture, engineering, medicine and aerospace. Given the design parameters of a single waterbomb cell, the global geometry of the origami tessellated shell at an intermediate state of folding is directly determined. Even though existing numerical methods of rigid-origami can be used to describe geometric forms, algebraic solutions of the waterbomb folding kinematics and tessellations reduce the algorithmic complexity and determine the range of admissible configurations exactly. The existing analytical solution for a symmetrically folded waterbomb cell and tessellation is extended to the case of a cell folded semi-symmetrically, i.e. a cell with a 180{\deg} rotation symmetry. The algebraic derivation provides the solution for the entire folding process. The resulting functional relationship between the design parameters and the 3D cell geometry of the folded waterbomb cell enables efficient studies of achievable shell geometries. This development facilitates a deeper understanding of the correspondence between the geometric parameters of a single waterbomb cell and the statically relevant geometric properties, i.e. the shell curvature and the effective cross-sectional height. The systematic description of this correspondence provides the basis for innovative design concepts using modern cementitious composites, e.g. textile-reinforced concrete, to produce thin-walled, high-performance, lightweight shells.
item.dc:creator: Sascha St\"uttgen, Homam Spartali, Alice C. Niemeyer, Rostislav Chudoba, Daniel Robertz

item.title: Diameter bounds for complexes that are close to flag or close to normal
item.description: arXiv:2611.08071v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Hirsch problem asks how large the diameter of the dual graph of a simplicial complex can be, in terms of its number of vertices. For normal complexes, the classical bounds are the Larman-Barnette bound, which is linear for fixed dimension, the Kalai-Kleitman bound, which is quasi-polynomial, and the Adiprasito-Benedetti bound n-d, which however holds only for flag complexes. After sharpening the Larman-Barnette and the Kalai-Kleitman bounds, we study how the three bounds deteriorate when flagness or normality is weakened. We give three ways to quantify the distance from flagness, and in each case we bound the diameter in a way that interpolates between the Adiprasito-Benedetti and the Larman-Barnette bounds. We also quantify the distance from normality by a parameter q, and obtain a bound that is a polynomial of degree q in n. Finally, we conjecture a statement on flag layered families that would imply an interpolation between the Adiprasito-Benedetti and the Kalai-Kleitman bounds.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Benedetti, Giuliamaria Menara

item.title: Quantifying discontinuity
item.description: arXiv:2511.07636v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a compact space $X$ that does not admit an embedding (an injective continuous function) into $\mathbb{R}^d$, we study the discontinuity that any injective function $X \to \mathbb{R}^d$ must have. To this end, we define a scale invariant modulus of discontinuity and obtain general lower bounds, thus obtaining quantified nonembeddability results of Haefliger--Weber type. Moreover, we establish analogous lower bounds for simplicial complexes that do not admit an almost $r$-embedding in $\mathbb{R}^d$, thus obtaining a quantified version of the topological Tverberg theorem.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Applied and Computational Topology 10, 31 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Henry Adams, Florian Frick, Michael Harrison, Nikola Sadovek, Matt Superdock

item.title: The microscopic weighting on a metric space
item.description: arXiv:2607.05349v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the microscopic weighting, a canonical signed measure of mass one that can be associated to almost any finite metric space. The microscopic weighting is obtained as the small-scale limit of the weightings used to define the magnitude function. We give general criteria for its existence, proving in particular that every finite space of strictly negative type admits a microscopic weighting; this includes every finite subset of Euclidean or hyperbolic space and every finite tree. Heuristically speaking, the microscopic weighting distributes its mass as widely as possible across a space, assigning greater weight to sparse or outlying regions and emphasizing points on the boundary. Indeed, we show that on a finite space of negative type the microscopic weighting can be characterized (when it exists) as an optimizing measure for an energy integral determined by the distance function. Alternatively, it can be characterized in terms of the geometry of the Schoenberg embedding. Each of these interpretations also clarifies the information carried by the derivative of the magnitude function at zero. Though our main focus in this paper is on finite metric spaces, we lay the groundwork to extend the theory to compact subsets of Euclidean space. In that setting, we observe that the microscopic weighting must be understood as a distribution rather than as a measure.
item.dc:creator: Emily Roff, Simon Willerton

item.title: Strong Negative Type of Star-shaped Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.20023v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Metric spaces of negative type (NT) and strong negative type (SNT) are fundamental in wide applications across computer science and statistics. It is well-known that spheres equipped with geodesic distance are of NT, and subsets of a sphere that contain at most one pair of antipodal points (e.g. an open hemisphere) are of SNT. In this paper, we extend these results to a class of star-shaped manifolds. By constructing a metric $d$ based on layer-wise radial projections, we prove that every star-shaped manifold, equipped with $d$, is of NT. Moreover, we prove that a subset of a star-shaped manifold is of SNT under certain injectivity and directional asymmetry conditions. In particular, for a subset of a single layer, it is of SNT if it contains exactly one point from each preimage of an open hemisphere (a fully directional asymmetry); moreover, it is of SNT if and only if it contains at most one opposite-directional pair. Finally, we prove that under similar conditions, SNT holds for almost and essentially star-shaped manifolds, and for those with incomplete radial coverage.
item.dc:creator: Hang Liu, Ziyan Xu

item.title: An elementary proof of a tangent-cone identity for rank-one planar Lipschitz maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.05161v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an elementary proof of a tangent-cone identity which might be known to specialists in geometric measure theory. It concerns Lipschitz mappings $g$ from the closed unit ball $B\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$. Let $x$ be an interior point of differentiability of $g$ at which $Dg(x)$ has rank one. If the upper one-dimensional Hausdorff density of $g(B)$ at $g(x)$ is at most one, then the tangent cone to $g(B)$ at $g(x)$ coincides with the image of $Dg(x)$. This property is used in the proof of rigidity for the four-gradient problem. We provide a detailed, self-contained proof based on differentiability, connectedness and elementary estimates for one-dimensional Hausdorff measure, without using advanced methods from geometric measure theory.
item.dc:creator: Igor Buchowiec

item.title: Isosceles sets and two-distance sets in Euclidean space
item.description: arXiv:2611.05421v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is isosceles if every three of its points form an isosceles triangle. Erd\H{o}s asked in 1946 for the largest size $\mathrm{iso}(d)$ of an isosceles set in $\mathbb{R}^d$; the answer was known for $d\le8$. Let $g(d)$ and $M(d)$ be the largest sizes of a two-distance set and of a spherical two-distance set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. We prove that $\mathrm{iso}(d)=\max\{g(d),M(d)+1,M(d-1)+3\}$ for every $d\ge2$, which reduces the problem to these two classical ones. With the recently determined values of $g(d)$ for $9\le d\le22$ we obtain $\mathrm{iso}(d)=\binom{d+1}{2}+1$ for $9\le d\le21$ and $\mathrm{iso}(22)=276$, and we show that the extremal set is unique: for $d\le21$ it is the set of midpoints of the edges of a regular simplex together with its centroid, and for $d=22$ it is the McLaughlin configuration together with its centre. For $10\le d\le22$ every isosceles set with more than $\binom d2+3$ points is a two-distance set or a spherical two-distance set together with its centre. The proofs start from Blokhuis' decomposition of isosceles sets into mutually orthogonal two-distance sets. Counting leaves one configuration open: a two-distance set with $\binom{d+1}{2}$ points in a hyperplane, the largest number allowed by Blokhuis' bound, together with two points that are mirror images of each other. We exclude it by showing that a two-distance set $T$ attaining Blokhuis' bound in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is unisolvent for quadratic polynomials and that, if $T$ lies on two concentric spheres, then apart from two exceptional cases its two layers are spherical $2$-designs whose sizes are determined by the radii. We also show that the squared distances of such a set are in ratio $(k-1):k$ with $(2k-1)^2\le n+1$ if $n\ge9$. Hence there is none for $9\le n\le23$, so that $g(23)\le299$ and $\mathrm{iso}(23)=\max\{g(23),278\}\le299$.
item.dc:creator: Hyunjun Yi

item.title: Uniqueness of the critical and supercritical Liouville quantum gravity metrics
item.description: arXiv:2110.00177v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that for each ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in [1,25)$, there is a unique metric associated with Liouville quantum gravity (LQG) with matter central charge ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M}$. An earlier series of works by Ding-Dub\'edat-Dunlap-Falconet, Gwynne-Miller, and others showed that such a metric exists and is unique in the subcritical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$, which corresponds to coupling constant $\gamma \in (0,2)$. The critical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} = 1$ corresponds to $\gamma=2$ and the supercritical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in (1,25)$ corresponds to $\gamma \in \mathbb C$ with $|\gamma| = 2$. Our metric is constructed as the limit of an approximation procedure called Liouville first passage percolation, which was previously shown to be tight for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in [1,25)$ by Ding and Gwynne (2020). In this paper, we show that the subsequential limit is uniquely characterized by a natural list of axioms. This extends the characterization of the LQG metric proven by Gwynne and Miller (2019) for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$ to the full parameter range $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,25)$. Our argument is substantially different from the proof of the characterization of the LQG metric for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$. In particular, the core part of the argument is simpler and does not use confluence of geodesics.
item.dc:creator: Jian Ding, Ewain Gwynne

item.title: HomID : Benchmarking Intrinsic Dimension Estimators on Homogenous Manifolds with Anisotropic Embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2510.01335v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The manifold hypothesis suggests that data lies on manifolds with smaller intrinsic dimension (ID) than their ambient dimension. However there is no empirical agreement on the estimates for ID from different estimators for realistic datasets. Thus it is important to test ID estimators (IDEs) with targeted stressors. In this work, we consider the role of anisotropy. To this end, we propose HomID, a collection of homogeneous spaces with anisotropic embedding, for benchmarking ID estimators. We observe that methods that perform well on standard benchmarks systematically degrade on HomID under identical resource allocation. We further observe that anisotropic distortion of such benchmarks also results in performance degradation. Finally, we demonstrate that controlled anisotropic distortions induce systematic shifts in the distributions on which these methods rely, providing a concrete mechanism for the resulting estimation errors in two particular IDEs. The code for the project is available at https://github.com/a-writes-code/homid
item.dc:creator: Aritra Das, Joseph T. Iosue, Victor V. Albert

item.title: Ropelength-Filtered Reidemeister Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2605.03350v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove relative smoothing with uniform reach control for one-parameter families of positive-reach $C^{1,1}$ knots and combine it with relative multijet transversality to obtain projection-generic regularization inside strict ropelength sublevels. Passing to a lifted Reidemeister multigraph reconstructs the admissible $\pi_0$ of every strict projection-framed ropelength sublevel, and the right-relaxed diagrammatic merge scale equals the geometric one. The normalised projection-framed sublevels are compact, so connected merge levels are attained. These degree-zero results are organized by a fibre cosheaf: a filtered relational cellular cosheaf of sets on the planar Reidemeister multigraph, whose stalks are strict fibre components and whose costalks are the relations realized by Reidemeister movies. The lifted multigraph is its Grothendieck construction, reconstruction is a descent statement, and the diagram image is its support. The diagram image computes merges exactly when no stalk is persistently separated, and a canonical flat coarsening is the coarsest diagram-indexed model that computes components. For amphichiral knots the spherical diagram image cannot detect mirror barriers, whereas the planar image can; no planar type of the standard diagrams of $4_1$ and $6_3$ is fixed by crossing switch. Symmetric hubs and finite certificates give upper bounds for mirror merges, and sign separators give lower bounds. For finite recognition we distinguish full rooted-ball occurrence, visibility in the monotone diagram-image filtration, and saturation. Every finite Reidemeister submultigraph becomes visible at a finite ropelength level, a visible saturated Barbensi-Celoria characteristic certificate determines the knot type up to mirroring, and a universal computable crossing-complexity bound controls visibility.
item.dc:creator: Makoto Ozawa
